thread:
incident-bot: 🚨 Incident detected: sudden GPU memory spike in us-west-1 inference pool causing container restarts (multiple hosts). Auto-page sent to oncall.
oncall-alex: Ack — I'm on it. Seeing repeated restarts on node pool inference-gpu-3. Containers show OOM during prefill on long-context requests.
eng-runtime-zhou: Can you paste the last container log? suspecting large prefill KV growth + fragmentation.
oncall-alex: Logs: ```E tensorflow: /dev/nvidia0: out of memory
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
CUDA error: out of memory (2)
[2026-01-12T15:12:34Z] oom-killer: kill process 4321 (model-server) score 764``` Also seeing `kvcache_eviction: miss_ratio=0.02, growth=+1.3GB` after a 30k token prompt.
eng-sre-maya: Node-level metric: GPU mem clipped >98% on 3 hosts. Pod restarts every ~90s. No system-level OOM, GPU driver shows CUDA_RESET on one host earlier.
eng-runtime-zhou: This smells like long-window prefill (user sent ~110k token context). Runtime didn't trim prefix because request flagged preserve_prefix=true. We have a mitigation: enable short-circuit trim for >64k tokens. Pushing a hotpatch to toggle trimming flag for the pool.
oncall-alex: Applying hotpatch to us-west-1 pool to enable aggressive prefix trimming and lower prefill batch size from 8->2. Rolling now.
incident-bot: deploy-bot: hotpatch rollout started by oncall-alex to cluster inference-gpu-3 (canary 10% -> 100%).
eng-sre-maya: Scaling the pool down: cordon 3 affected nodes and move new traffic to warm-fallback pool in us-west-2. K8s commands run:
```kubectl cordon gpu-node-12
kubectl drain gpu-node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
kubectl scale deployment inference-pool-uswest1 --replicas=0``` 
cust-success-james: Customer ops: A handful of power users on enterprise account ACME saw 503s and increased latency. I've DM'd them initial note and will send a status update once we have mitigation confirmation.
eng-runtime-zhou: Canary shows immediate drop in OOMs. Patch forced trimming cut memory usage ~1.6GB per pod. Rolling to remaining nodes.
oncall-alex: After roll, restarts stopped on canary nodes. Full roll at 15:22 UTC. Monitoring for regressions.
product-erin: Any impact to feature parity with trimming enabled? Need to flag to customers that extremely long context may be truncated; we'll surface in release notes.
eng-runtime-zhou: Trimming is a last-resort short-term mitigation — we'll follow up with a longer-term KV compression + LRU eviction in the runtime. Filing a follow-up RFC.
eng-sre-maya: Handoff to night oncall @oncall-jordan in 30m with runbook: https://go/runbooks/gpu-prefill-memory-spike. Please monitor 5xx rate and GPU mem >90% alerts.
oncall-alex: Oncall handoff: @oncall-jordan — summary: hotpatch enabled aggressive trimming and reduced batch size, cordoned 3 nodes, traffic shifted to fallback pool; customer ACME impacted with transient 503s. Next steps: watch for comeback of OOMs and any double-scaling events.
cust-success-james: I'll send ACME a short update: root cause is large-context prefill memory spike; mitigation in place; ETA for full fix TBD. Asked if they want proactive throttling for high-token requests.
incident-bot: incident-logger: incident created #INC-2026-1723, severity: P2, owner: oncall-alex, timeline attached.
oncall-alex: Closing notes: immediate mitigation successful, customer notified, engineering follow-up actions: (1) runtime KV LRU work (2) throttling policy for >64k token requests (3) better circuit-breaker to reject preserve_prefix on extremely long contexts. Passing to post-incident triage.
